Thanks Alice! Looking forward to connecting with everyone here and learning more about the new 2025.Q4 features.

This sounds like a Service Access Policy issue. In the Q4 release, there were some tightened defaults. Check Control Panel > Security > Service Access Policies and ensure your custom endpoints are explicitly allowed.
I tried checking the policies but they look the same as before. Is there anything else that could be blocking the request?
Make sure you also verify the OAuth2 scope assignments. If you're using a Client Extension to call the API, the scope needs to be correctly mapped in the User Account or Service Account.
Have you enabled DEBUG logging for com.liferay.portal.security.sso.saml? It usually provides a very specific reason for the 'Invalid SAML Response' error in the logs.
I've seen this with Azure AD specifically. It often comes down to the NameID format. Make sure it's set to persistent or emailAddress depending on your Liferay configuration.
For Custom Objects, sometimes a simple re-index isn't enough. Try going to Control Panel > Search > Index Actions and perform a Full Reindex for that specific object type.
I already did a full reindex. Could it be related to the indexable property in the Object definition itself?

For simple CRUD and internal data, Objects is definitely the way to go. It's much faster to set up and integrates natively with the UI. Use Service Builder only if you need complex relational logic or custom SQL.
I agree. We recently switched to Objects for a small project and saved about 40% in development time since we didn't have to write any boilerplate DTOs or persistence logic.
What are your JVM heap settings? If you're using Docker, make sure your -Xmx is set to at least 75% of the container memory to avoid the kernel killing the process.
We discovered that the Document Preview generation was the culprit. For files over 100MB, it was consuming massive amounts of memory. Disabling previews for those file types fixed it.
I'd love to see this too! My eyes definitely feel the strain after 8 hours in the Control Panel. A native dark mode would be a huge win for UX.
There is actually an active feature request for this on the Liferay Product Board. I suggest everyone go there and upvote it to get it prioritized!
I've seen this as well. It seems to be a specific rendering issue in Safari's WebKit engine when handling nested flexboxes in the editor view.
Confirmed. Switching to Chrome or Firefox is a temporary workaround, but the fix is scheduled for the next monthly update.
Using Redis for session clustering is a must for high-traffic sites. It significantly reduces the database load compared to using the default database-backed session store.
Don't forget about CDN integration. Offloading static assets like JS and CSS to a CDN like Cloudflare or Akamai is the single biggest performance boost you can get.
Check your client-extension.yaml. If the type or portletCategoryName is misconfigured, the extension might deploy but never actually render on the page.
Look at the browser console for 404 errors. It's possible the build artifacts weren't correctly uploaded to the static host during your CI/CD pipeline.
Is there a specific version of the SAML module you're using? I remember a bug in the 5.0.1 version that caused similar issues with encrypted assertions.
Great point! I updated to 5.0.2 and that resolved the 'Invalid SAML Response' error. Thanks for the tip!
For the search issue, check the search-request-processor logs. It will show you the actual query being sent to Elasticsearch.
I found the issue in the logs — the field name was being prefixed with expando__ unexpectedly. Corrected the mapping and it works now.
Regarding Objects vs Service Builder: don't forget that Objects automatically provides Headless APIs, which is a huge advantage for modern frontends.
Exactly. Trying to wrap Service Builder in a custom REST layer is just extra work you don't need anymore.
For memory leaks, I highly recommend using VisualVM or YourKit to take a heap dump. It's the only way to be 100% sure what's holding onto memory.
We used Eclipse MAT to analyze the dump and it pointed right at the image processing library. Updating to the latest security patch fixed it.
I've also noticed that the 'Publish' button in the fragment editor sometimes disappears in Safari when the screen width is exactly 1024px.
Yes! That's the breakpoint where the sidebar toggles. It seems the button gets pushed under the overlay. Good catch.
For high traffic, make sure you tune your HikariCP connection pool. The default settings are often too low for high-concurrency environments.
I increased maximumPoolSize to 50 and saw a significant decrease in request latency during peak hours. Thanks!
If your Client Extension isn't loading, verify that the CORS settings in Liferay allow the domain where your static assets are hosted.
The CORS configuration was the issue. I added our CDN domain to the allowed origins and the dynamic import started working.
